On a short finish, rules for the front-counter team
This section explains the steps for the whole desk

Companion Animal Travel Desk intake and handoff
The purpose of this section is to keep animal travel smooth, calm, and consistent for every guest. Keep your voice easy, check documents without rushing, and make sure each traveler knows where the next step happens. If a pet arrives stressed, give the owner a steady update and move one step at a time.

For lounge and relief-area questions, share the approved details only and let the system records do the rest. <<FACT F020>> When a traveler asks for the Port Isolde lounge, stay with the approved handoff path and avoid guessing. <<FACT F003>> If someone needs help reaching the Merrowgate relief area, use the current access note and keep the exchange brief. <<FACT F017>>

When a carrier looks damaged, a tag is missing, or an animal seems unwell, pause the check-in and call the senior coordinator right away. Offer water, shade, and a quiet place when available, and keep the owner informed in plain language. If a case feels uncertain, do not improvise. Follow the calm stepwise review, log what you saw, and wait for the next instruction.

Every animal receives patient attention from trained staff, and the front desk should support that standard from first greeting to final handoff. If you need a final decision, contact the senior coordinator or the operations desk for guidance.
